Recover stale active job records using scheduler accounting

Source: R/project_recovery.R
reconcile_project_jobs.Rd

Preview scheduler observations with the default dry_run = TRUE. With dry_run = FALSE, only confirmed scheduler failures and cancellations update active database rows. Missing accounting records and unavailable schedulers never authorize retries. Scheduler completion alone does not establish that required outputs or completion manifests are valid; these rows are returned with action VERIFY_OUTPUTS and remain unchanged.

Usage

reconcile_project_jobs(input = getwd(), dry_run = TRUE)

Arguments

input

Project configuration, YAML file, or project directory.

dry_run

Preview changes without updating SQLite. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

A data frame with database and scheduler states, proposed actions, and an applied flag for each active tracked job. UPDATE_TERMINAL_FAILURE proposes a confirmed failure/cancellation repair; CONFIRM_OUTCOME and VERIFY_OUTPUTS require further investigation and leave records unchanged. Other records have action UNCHANGED.

Details

The recorded end time for a recovered failure is the reconciliation time when no worker end time exists. This function submits and cancels no jobs. Unbound uncertain submissions require resolve_project_submission().

Unlike a run_project() preflight, this explicit operation reviews all active tracked jobs in the project, not just the scope of a new request. Its preview contacts the scheduler even though it does not update SQLite. Neither mode reads imaging files or verifies completed outputs. Unknown legacy tracking states and dependency-blocked allocations without confirmed scheduler termination are included. For a dependency-blocked row, confirmed failure/cancellation records scheduler_terminal_state but retains logical status FAILED_BY_EXT; run-based retries still require include_blocked = TRUE to select that work.

For future runs, tracked submission errors stop the submission loop at the first failure, retaining scheduler stdout and stderr beside the job manifest. Explicit supported Slurm policy/request rejections are retryable; transport errors remain uncertain. Retries automatically reconcile matching active attempts against confirmed scheduler failures before checking duplicates.

Keep logs/runs with the tracking database: it contains the evidence needed for recovery. For input problems, finish conversion before preprocessing, run run_bids_validation() and inspect its report before launching a cohort. Changing the output directory does not repair shared BIDS inputs. Never remove or rename anatomical files solely to suppress validator errors; determine which acquisitions and derived files should be retained first.

See also

inspect_project() for status, diagnose_project() for recovery guidance, and resolve_project_submission() for uncertain acceptance. See vignette("diagnosing_pipeline", package = "BrainGnomes") for the recovery decision guide and automatic preflight workflow.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
scfg <- load_project("/project/my_study")
recovery <- reconcile_project_jobs(scfg)
recovery[, c("job_id", "status", "scheduler_status", "action", "applied")]
# After reviewing the observations, explicitly apply confirmed repairs.
reconcile_project_jobs(scfg, dry_run = FALSE)
} # }
